sam kim: Hey folks — Sam here, first day! Trying to run my first Buildkite pipeline but the checkout step keeps failing with `Permission denied (publickey)` and Buildkite shows a 128 exit. Anyone seen this for new joiners?

lena (infra): welcome Sam :wave:  Usually that's either a missing GH org invite or the pipeline's SSH key isn't set. Did you accept the org invite and grant the GitHub App access?

sam kim: I accepted the invite and I can view the repo in the web UI. GH showed a prompt about the Buildkite app but I think I clicked accept. The Buildkite UI shows the pipeline but the agent logs say: \`git@github.com: Permission denied (publickey).\`

matt (infra-lead): can you paste the exact agent log? also, are you running the build locally (agent on laptop) or on our shared fleet?

sam kim: On shared fleet (our default). Here is the checkout snippet from the agent: 

```
+ git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/infra-config.git
Cloning into 'infra-config'...
Permission denied (publickey).
fatal: Could not read from remote repository.
\nPlease make sure you have the correct access rights
and the repository exists.
```

\nci-bot: Buildkite: Step "checkout" failed (exit status 128)\n\nlena (infra): okay that log is the classic SSH auth failure. Two common causes: (1) pipeline expects a repo-scoped deploy key / secret and doesn't have it, or (2) agent doesn't have any identities loaded into ssh-agent (Agent admitted failure...). can you run `ssh-add -l` on the agent host?

sam kim: I can't directly ssh into the fleet host, but I can run a quick job with a debug command in the pipeline. Running `ssh -v git@github.com` inside a debug step produced: 

```
debug1: identity file /root/.ssh/id_rsa type -1
debug1: No such identity: /root/.ssh/id_rsa
debug1: identity file /root/.ssh/id_ed25519 type -1
debug1: No such identity: /root/.ssh/id_ed25519
Agent admitted failure to sign using the key.
```

lena (infra): that output means the agent process has nothing to sign with. Our fleet normally installs a repo deploy key into the pipeline's environment variable (BUILDKITE_DEPLOY_KEY) and a checkout hook writes it to /root/.ssh/id_deploy and calls `ssh-add`. Sounds like that step didn't run or the secret is missing for this pipeline.

olivia (eng): fwiw we've been rolling out a tighter repo grant scope so some older pipelines lost access when we rotated the deploy key. Sam, what's the pipeline slug? I'll check secrets access.

sam kim: pipeline is `infra/check-config` (slug infra-check-config).

matt (infra-lead): @olivia can you confirm the secret is present? Also check the pipeline settings -> permissions -> repository. Sometimes the GH App needs explicit repo access even if the user can see it.

olivia (eng): checking now... looks like the pipeline lost the secret after the rotation — BUt the secret exists in the team vault, I reattached it to the pipeline and toggled the "Expose for Pull Requests" off. Also added an SSH known_hosts line to the script: `ssh-keyscan github.com >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts` since the build container was failing strict host checking.

sam kim: nice, thanks. I re-ran the job and now the checkout gets a bit further but fails with `Agent admitted failure to sign using the key` still.

lena (infra): two more checks: (1) confirm the hook that writes the env var into a file then `chmod 600` and runs `ssh-add /root/.ssh/id_deploy` — sometimes the agent user is root but the socket is under another user, causing sign failures. (2) ensure the Buildkite agent process can reach the ssh-agent socket — check `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` env var is set for the build job. Can you paste the debug step env dump?

sam kim: debug env dump: `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` is empty in the debug container. I see in the pipeline yaml we do a wrapper script that expects `ssh-agent` to be started by the agent itself. Perhaps the managed fleet changed the wrapper recently.

matt (infra-lead): thanks — that's the kicker. I pushed a fix to the fleet bootstrap: the Buildkite job wrapper wasn't launching ssh-agent for ephemeral containers when using the new sandbox runtime. I've re-deployed the wrapper (PR #142) and restarted a subset of agents. Can you trigger a new build?

sam kim: kicked off another build...

ci-bot: Buildkite: Step "checkout" started

ci-bot: Buildkite: Step "checkout" passed

sam kim: It passed! :tada: thanks everyone. Two tiny docs notes: 1) onboarding checklist should mention accepting the GH App and verifying pipeline secrets, 2) add a troubleshooting snippet for "Agent admitted failure to sign" to the ops runbook.

lena (infra): excellent — will add a short note to onboarding and the runbook. welcome aboard, Sam :coffee:
